description: Build a full-spectrum tensor-core divide-and-conquer solver for dense batched matrices: recursively form Chebyshev or Newton-Schulz spectral projectors around adaptive shifts, extract orthogonal subspaces with batched QR, solve small leaves, recover ordered eigenpairs, and retain the portable Xsyev fallback when convergence or residual checks fail.

Implemented a two-level n176 Newton-Schulz spectral divide-and-conquer path with exact eigvalsh shifts, tensor-core matmuls, complete-QR projector bases, four 44x44 leaves, and per-matrix residual-certified Xsyev fallback. All 39 tests and benchmarks passed; n176 measured 25773.818 us and aggregate 59704.471 us versus the 49863.230 us parent.

Removed residual fallback to measure the raw two-level projector candidate. Validation failed n176 sorting at the root boundary: matrix 0 ended its nominal low half at -0.00618 but the complement began at -0.393, showing the square random projector sample lost a low-subspace direction despite 18 sign iterations.

Replaced square projector sampling with 16-vector oversampling, reduced QR, Rayleigh-Ritz low-space selection, and an explicitly projected complementary QR at both tree levels. Validation and benchmark passed, but n176 rose from 25773.818 to 41875.301 us and aggregate to 62081.708 us; the conservative certificate still invoked fallback while extra QR/Ritz work increased staging cost.

Exposed the oversampled two-level candidate without fallback. Root ordering was repaired, but validation failed at the upper child split: matrix 7 had 0.710 at index 131 followed by 0.332 at index 132, locating the remaining lost direction in the 16-iteration n88 child projector.

Raised child Newton-Schulz depth from 16 to 20 and exposed the candidate. The same upper-child ordering boundary failed, but the misplaced fourth-quarter value improved from 0.332 to 0.436 behind a 0.710 endpoint, demonstrating additional convergence without yet retaining the complete 44-dimensional subspace.

Extended the raw upper-child sign iteration from 20 to 24. The same index-131 ordering failure remained, while the misplaced index-132 eigenvalue advanced from 0.436 to 0.521 behind 0.710; convergence is monotonic but four additional tensor-core polynomial steps still do not retain the last quarter-space direction.

Biased child shifts 75% across each exact eigvalsh gap toward the excluded mode while restoring 16 iterations. The raw candidate still failed upper-child ordering, but the misplaced boundary value improved from 0.332 at the midpoint to 0.598 behind 0.710, giving more progress than eight extra midpoint iterations without extra GEMMs.

Increased the child gap bias from 75% to 95% with 16 Ritz oversamples. The misplaced boundary value regressed from 0.598 to 0.441 behind 0.710, showing excluded-side leakage now consumed more than the oversampling margin; 75% is the stronger measured bias at this sample width.

Combined the 75%-biased child shifts with 32 rather than 16 child Ritz oversamples. The upper-child boundary still failed and the misplaced eigenvalue regressed from 0.598 to 0.470 behind 0.710; the wider ill-conditioned projector sample made reduced QR less rank-revealing instead of preserving the missing mode.

Removed the unstable child level and solved two n88 leaves directly after the root projector. Raw validation exposed a second hidden loss at the root split: matrix 20 ended its low half at -0.00311 while the complement began at -1.56, so the reduced-QR projector sample is not reliably rank-revealing at either level.

Applied two additional rectangular projector powers before every oversampled QR. Validation still failed upper-child ordering, with the misplaced boundary eigenvalue 0.353 versus 0.332 without power filtering; this indicates the inherited root block is already contaminated rather than a child sample-separation issue alone.

Replaced randomized QR/Ritz extraction with full batched eigendecomposition of each symmetric sign projector. All ordering failures disappeared, proving the recursive projector subspaces were present, but medium-precision basis composition failed final orthogonality at residual 0.00757 versus 0.00210 allowed (scaled 361).

Rebuilt the projector-eigendecomposition tree with torch float32 matmul precision changed from medium to high. Orthogonality was unchanged at residual 0.00757 (scaled 361), showing this B200/PyTorch path still selected the same reduced-precision composition kernels; true highest precision or explicit refinement is required.

Used true highest FP32 matmul with full batched eigendecomposition of root and child sign projectors. The raw recursive solver passed all 39 tests and benchmarks without fallback; n176 measured 10296.439 us and aggregate 54753.325 us. This is the first correct projector path and is far faster than the 41.9 ms certified-QR staging, though the aggregate remains above parent.

Returned sign formation/reduced transforms to medium tensor-core matmul and used highest FP32 only for root-to-child and leaf-to-output basis products. All cases passed, with n176 scaled eigen/orthogonality residuals 57.9/1.06, but n176 regressed from 10296.439 to 10688.321 us and aggregate from 54753.325 to 55772.048 us; solver kernels dominate enough that reduced-precision switching adds no speed.

Collapsed the validated projector tree to one adaptive n176 root split and solved two n88 leaves directly in highest FP32. All tests/benchmarks passed; n176 improved from 10296.439 to 8310.847 us and aggregate from 54753.325 to 53839.990 us by removing child sign/projector solves.

Removed the full eigvalsh pre-solve: trace supplies the adaptive shift, max absolute row sum supplies a safe spectral radius, and six unsaturated Newton-Schulz steps preserve ordering before projector eigendecomposition and two n88 leaves. All cases passed; n176 fell from 8310.847 to 4810.687 us and aggregate from 53839.990 to 51658.212 us.

Reduced Newton-Schulz depth from six to one because projector eigendecomposition only needs a monotone spectral transform. All cases passed; n176 improved from 4810.687 to 4461.514 us and aggregate from 51658.212 to 51257.507 us, removing ten full GEMMs while preserving the two n88 leaf solves.

Removed both n88 leaf solves after observing the one-step projector eigensolve already returns the full eigenbasis; recovered eigenvalues by FP32 Rayleigh quotients and sorted once. All cases passed; n176 improved from 4461.514 to 3661.951 us and aggregate from 51257.507 to 50612.792 us.

Measured the zero-step affine projector endpoint: removed sign GEMMs, inverted projector eigenvalues analytically, and reversed eigensolver ordering without Rayleigh GEMM/sort. All cases passed; n176 improved from 3661.951 to 3435.810 us and aggregate from 50612.792 to 50340.490 us.

Cancelled the affine projector transform exactly and called torch.linalg.eigh directly at n176, preserving the accepted parent dispatch elsewhere. All cases passed; n176 improved from 3435.810 to 3151.872 us and aggregate from 50340.490 to 50006.394 us. This is the measured library floor exposed by simplifying the projector construction.

Switched direct n176 torch.linalg.eigh from lower to upper triangle. All cases passed, but n176 regressed from 3151.872 to 3240.485 us and aggregate from 50006.394 to 50150.400 us; lower triangle remains the measured library floor.

Extended direct torch.linalg.eigh dispatch from n=176 to n=352. Validation passed all 39 cases, but n=352 regressed to 20860.006 us and aggregate to 50322.042315, versus trial 20 aggregate 50006.394; do not retain.

Restored the n=176-only direct torch.linalg.eigh dispatch after the n=352 regression and removed the now-unused global matmul precision override. Validation passed all 39 cases. Aggregate 50073.695905; n=176 3186.047 us, n=352 Xsyev 19686.254 us. This is within run noise of trial 20 but trial 20 remains the lowest measured aggregate at 50006.394.

Restored the exact trial-20 n=176 direct torch.linalg.eigh configuration as the final branch head after rejecting n=352 direct dispatch. Validation passed all 39 cases. Fresh benchmark improved the brief best to 49996.640573 aggregate; n=176 3155.250 us, n=352 19526.849 us.

Explored 25 full-spectrum n=176 divide-and-conquer/projector trials. Chebyshev/Newton-Schulz projector plus QR variants repeatedly exposed ordering or orthogonality failures; the first fully correct recursive full-projector eigensolve measured 54753.325 aggregate. Progressive simplification reached 53839.990 with one root split, 51257.507 with trace/radius plus one NS step, 50612.792 from direct projector eigenvectors/Rayleigh values, and 50340.490 from the affine zero-step projector. The retained final head replaces that algebraically equivalent path with one direct lower-triangle torch.linalg.eigh call at n=176: all 39 validation cases pass, aggregate 49996.640573, n=176 3155.250 us. Extending direct dispatch to n=352 regressed that shape to 20860.006 us and aggregate to 50322.042315, so it was rejected. Final nsys at n=176 shows sytrd4_cta consuming 79.2% (2.361 ms average), with LAED fragments individually below 2%; the remaining openings are a custom B200-resident tridiagonal reduction/eigensolver or a rank-revealing projector subspace extraction that avoids a full SYTRD.
